name: Man Parrish
hook: Built a club-floor anthem almost entirely out of a drum machine and two synthesizers, months ahead of 'Planet Rock' making that the whole point.
blurb: Parrish grew up in Brooklyn on funk and experimental electronic music, then built 'Hip Hop, Be Bop (Don't Stop)' in 1982 almost entirely from a Roland TR-808 and a couple of synthesizers, with barely any vocal. It came out before 'Planet Rock' and is one of electro's very first records. It was built on the same machine but came from downtown New York's club and disco underground rather than from the Bronx sound systems, on almost exactly the same timeline. Genres rarely have one clean starting point, and electro clearly has two.

signatureTracks.title: Hip Hop, Be Bop (Don't Stop)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Built almost entirely from a TR-808 and synthesizers with minimal vocal, and among the earliest records to put the 808 at the center rather than in the background.

signatureTracks.title: Male Stripper
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A 1986 hi-NRG single credited to Man 2 Man meet Man Parrish, a long way from the Bronx electro of his first record.
